speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe the appearance of the rash on your trunk and extremities, and when did it first appear relative to your fever?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the facial rash have a "slapped cheek" appearance, and does the trunk rash appear lacy or net-like? I would also like to know if she has had any contact with other sick children recently. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical presentation of a slapped-cheek facial rash followed by a lacy, net-like rash on the trunk and extremities is classic for Erythema Infectiosum. DIAGNOSIS READY: Fifth Disease (Erythema Infectiosum) caused by Parvovirus B19
